function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output

function.name: search_output

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. message.content: Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Wait, my fix was wrong - let me reconsider. Let me re-check the logic: originally `if not (end is not None): eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(...); tlist.group_tokens(...)`. This means group_tokens was only called when end IS None (the "not matching" search failed to find anything after comment, meaning the comment extends to end of list). In that branch, eidx (from token_not_matching, which would be None since nothing matched beyond end of list) gets reassigned via token_prev - which should give a valid token_prev before idx=eidx(None). But token_prev with idx=None returns None,None per sql.py line 301-302. That's the actual bug! The eidx is None when end is None, so token_prev(None,...) returns (None,None), causing group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, None) -> None+True crashes.

So my fix (inverting the condition) is wrong - it now only groups when end is NOT None (found a non-comment token after), but doesn't handle the case where comment goes to end of tlist at all! That seems backwards too. Let me look at this more carefully before finalizing.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Wait, my fix was wrong - let me reconsider. Let me re-check the logic: originally `if not (end is not None): eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(...); tlist.group_tokens(...)`. This means group_tokens was only called when end IS None (the "not matching" search failed to find anything after comment, meaning the comment extends to end of list). In that branch, eidx (from token_not_matching, which would be None since nothing matched beyond end of list) gets reassigned via token_prev - which should give a valid token_prev before idx=eidx(None). But token_prev with idx=None returns None,None per sql.py line 301-302. That's the actual bug! The eidx is None when end is None, so token_prev(None,...) returns (None,None), causing group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, None) -> None+True crashes.

So my fix (inverting the condition) is wrong - it now only groups when end is NOT None (found a non-comment token after), but doesn't handle the case where comment goes to end of tlist at all! That seems backwards too. Let me look at this more carefully before finalizing.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Wait, my fix was wrong - let me reconsider. Let me re-check the logic: originally `if not (end is not None): eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(...); tlist.group_tokens(...)`. This means group_tokens was only called when end IS None (the "not matching" search failed to find anything after comment, meaning the comment extends to end of list). In that branch, eidx (from token_not_matching, which would be None since nothing matched beyond end of list) gets reassigned via token_prev - which should give a valid token_prev before idx=eidx(None). But token_prev with idx=None returns None,None per sql.py line 301-302. That's the actual bug! The eidx is None when end is None, so token_prev(None,...) returns (None,None), causing group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, None) -> None+True crashes.

So my fix (inverting the condition) is wrong - it now only groups when end is NOT None (found a non-comment token after), but doesn't handle the case where comment goes to end of tlist at all! That seems backwards too. Let me look at this more carefully before finalizing.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

Fixed the bug: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(), the condition `if not (end is not None):` was inverted — it should only group tokens into a Comment when `end` IS found (not None); when end is None it should fall through to use token_prev. This inversion caused `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` to sometimes be called with eidx=None (when end was not None after token_prev lookup was skipped), or caused group_tokens to receive None end in the None branch, leading to `end + include_end` raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` in sql.py's group_tokens. I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact

function.name: note

function.name: read_note

I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so the token_prev/group_tokens call only happens when a valid end token exists. Now running tests to confirm the fix resolves the regression.

structured_output.content:
Root cause confirmed: in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py, group_comments() had an inverted condition `if not (end is not None):` instead of `if end is not None:`. This caused the function to call `tlist.token_prev(eidx, ...)` and `tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)` precisely in the case where `eidx` was None (no trailing token found after the comment run), so `token_prev(None, ...)` returned `(None, None)`, and `group_tokens(..., end=None)` then computed `end_idx = end + include_end` => `None + True`, raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'`. This matches the reported regression (strip_comments relies on sql.Comment being grouped correctly before StripCommentsFilter runs).

I corrected the condition to `if end is not None:`, so grouping only happens when a valid terminating token index was found (the normal/expected case), restoring the original correct behavior. I verified via direct Python calls (no `TypeError` crashes) that:
- single-line `--` comments are stripped correctly, preserving line breaks (`select *-- comment\nfrom foo` -> `select *\nfrom foo`)
- multiple single-line comments are stripped
- multi-line `/* ... */` comments are stripped
- SQL hint comments (`/*+ ... */`, presumably also `--+`) are preserved as required
- trailing comments at the end of a statement are stripped without crashing
- normal formatting/reindenting unaffected by the change

This checkout has no `tests/` directory to run the hidden upstream suite against, so I validated with targeted manual smoke tests via `python -c`. The one-line fix is minimal and targeted, consistent with upstream's known-correct implementation of `group_comments`.

No other code paths were touched.

arguments.summary: Fixed regression in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(): the condition guarding the token_prev/group_tokens call was inverted (`if not (end is not None):`), causing group_tokens to be invoked with a None end index when no trailing non-comment token was found, which raised TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool' inside sql.py's group_tokens (end_idx = end + include_end). Corrected the condition to `if end is not None:` so grouping of Comment tokens only proceeds when a valid end token was located, matching the intended/original logic. Verified via manual sqlparse.format(..., strip_comments=True) smoke tests covering single-line comments, multi-line comments, SQL hints (preserved), trailing comments, and comment-only / newline-adjacent cases — no crashes, and hint-preservation plus comment stripping work as expected. Also confirmed normal reindent/formatting paths unaffected.
